name: VL53L1X time-of-flight distance sensor
description: ST FlightSense time-of-flight sensor that times 940 nm laser pulses to measure absolute distance from 4 cm up to 4 m, read in millimetres over I2C (up to 400 kHz) at address 0x29 with 16-bit register addresses. The bare chip runs from 2.6–3.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit VL53L1X Time of Flight Distance Sensor breakout (product 3967; 6-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, GPIO, XSHUT plus two STEMMA QT ports) with a 2.8 V regulator and level shifting, so VIN takes 3–5 V.
eli5: It flashes a tiny invisible laser and times how long the light takes to bounce back, which tells you how far away something is, up to about 4 metres.

buildNotes: Peel off the protective film over the sensor window before use, or readings will be wrong.

Registers have 16-bit addresses: send the address MSB first, then data. The driver waits for boot (0x00E5 bit 0), loads ST's 91-byte default configuration to 0x002D–0x0087 and starts continuous ranging with 0x40 in 0x0087.
Each range is 16-bit mm at 0x0096; range status 0x0089 (low 5 bits) must be 9 for a valid reading. Write 0x01 to 0x0086 after every read or the result will not update.
Every VL53L1X starts at address 0x29. For several on one bus hold their XSHUT pins low, release them one at a time and set a new address (register 0x0001).
Long mode reaches 3.6–4 m in the dark but only about 0.7 m in strong sunlight; use short mode (about 1.3 m) outdoors. Under 4 cm the distance is not accurate.
Ranging peaks at about 40 mA; keep power wires short or add a 10 µF capacitor near VIN.

driver.code:
# VL53L1X time-of-flight distance sensor (ST), MicroPython driver.
# Follows ST's Ultra Lite Driver (ULD, STSW-IMG009) register sequence: 16-bit register
# addresses, the 91-byte default configuration written to 0x2D..0x87, continuous ranging
# started with 0x40 in SYSTEM__MODE_START, data-ready polled on GPIO__TIO_HV_STATUS.
import time

_I2C_SLAVE_DEVICE_ADDRESS = 0x0001
_VHV_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_LOOP_BOUND = 0x0008
_GPIO_HV_MUX_CTRL = 0x0030
_GPIO_TIO_HV_STATUS = 0x0031
_PHASECAL_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP = 0x004B
_RANGE_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_A_HI = 0x005E
_RANGE_CONFIG_VCSEL_PERIOD_A = 0x0060
_RANGE_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_B_HI = 0x0061
_RANGE_CONFIG_VCSEL_PERIOD_B = 0x0063
_RANGE_CONFIG_VALID_PHASE_HIGH = 0x0069
_SYSTEM_INTERMEASUREMENT_PERIOD = 0x006C
_SD_CONFIG_WOI_SD0 = 0x0078
_SD_CONFIG_INITIAL_PHASE_SD0 = 0x007A
_SYSTEM_INTERRUPT_CLEAR = 0x0086
_SYSTEM_MODE_START = 0x0087
_RESULT_RANGE_STATUS = 0x0089
_RESULT_RANGE_MM = 0x0096   # RESULT__FINAL_CROSSTALK_CORRECTED_RANGE_MM_SD0, 16-bit, mm
_RESULT_OSC_CALIBRATE_VAL = 0x00DE
_FIRMWARE_SYSTEM_STATUS = 0x00E5
_IDENTIFICATION_MODEL_ID = 0x010F  # 0xEA, then module type 0xCC at 0x0110

# ST ULD default configuration for registers 0x2D..0x87 (91 bytes).
_DEFAULT_CONFIG = bytes((
    0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x00, 0x02, 0x08,  # 0x2D..0x34
    0x00, 0x08, 0x10, 0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x35..0x3C
    0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x0F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x3D..0x44
    0x00, 0x20, 0x0B, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0x0A, 0x21,  # 0x45..0x4C
    0x00, 0x00, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC8,  # 0x4D..0x54
    0x00, 0x00, 0x38, 0xFF, 0x01, 0x00, 0x08, 0x00,  # 0x55..0x5C
    0x00, 0x01, 0xCC, 0x0F, 0x01, 0xF1, 0x0D, 0x01,  # 0x5D..0x64
    0x68, 0x00, 0x80, 0x08, 0xB8, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x65..0x6C
    0x00, 0x0F, 0x89, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x6D..0x74
    0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x0F, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x0E, 0x00,  # 0x75..0x7C
    0x00, 0x02, 0xC7, 0xFF, 0x9B, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x7D..0x84
    0x01, 0x00, 0x00,                                # 0x85..0x87
))

# Timing budget (ms) -> (RANGE_CONFIG__TIMEOUT_MACROP_A, _B) words, from the ST ULD.
_TB_SHORT = {15: (0x001D, 0x0027), 20: (0x0051, 0x006E), 33: (0x00D6, 0x006E),
             50: (0x01AE, 0x01E8), 100: (0x02E1, 0x0388), 200: (0x03E1, 0x0496),
             500: (0x0591, 0x05C1)}
_TB_LONG = {20: (0x001E, 0x0022), 33: (0x0060, 0x006E), 50: (0x00AD, 0x00C6),
            100: (0x01CC, 0x01EA), 200: (0x02D9, 0x02F8), 500: (0x048F, 0x04A4)}

# RESULT__RANGE_STATUS (low 5 bits) -> ULD range status (0 = valid).
_STATUS = {9: 0, 6: 1, 4: 2, 8: 3, 5: 4, 3: 5, 19: 6, 7: 7, 12: 9, 18: 10, 22: 11, 23: 12, 13: 13}


class VL53L1X:
    def __init__(self, i2c, address=0x29, io_2v8=True, timeout_ms=1000):
        """io_2v8=True suits breakouts whose SDA/SCL/GPIO1 are pulled up to the 2.8 V AVDD
        (Adafruit, Pololu, most clones). Use False only for a bare chip with 1.8 V I/O."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = address
        self.timeout_ms = timeout_ms
        self.range_status = 255
        mid = self._rd(_IDENTIFICATION_MODEL_ID, 2)
        if mid[0] != 0xEA or mid[1] != 0xCC:
            raise OSError('VL53L1X not found (model id %02X%02X, expected EACC)' % (mid[0], mid[1]))
        self._wait(lambda: self._rd(_FIRMWARE_SYSTEM_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x01, 'boot')
        cfg = bytearray(_DEFAULT_CONFIG)
        if io_2v8:
            cfg[0x2E - 0x2D] |= 0x01  # I2C pads pulled up at AVDD
            cfg[0x2F - 0x2D] |= 0x01  # GPIO pad pulled up at AVDD
        self._wr(0x2D, cfg)
        # ULD SensorInit: one ranging to settle VHV, then stop.
        self.start_ranging()
        self._wait(self.data_ready, 'first ranging')
        self.clear_interrupt()
        self.stop_ranging()
        self._wr(_VHV_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_LOOP_BOUND, b'\x09')  # two bounds VHV
        self._wr(0x000B, b'\x00')  # start VHV from the previous temperature
        self.set_distance_mode(2)
        self.set_timing_budget(50)

    # ---- low level: 16-bit register addresses, big-endian data ----
    def _wr(self, reg, data):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes(((reg >> 8) & 0xFF, reg & 0xFF)) + bytes(data))

    def _rd(self, reg, n):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes(((reg >> 8) & 0xFF, reg & 0xFF)))
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    def _wr16(self, reg, v):
        self._wr(reg, bytes(((v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF)))

    def _wait(self, cond, what):
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not cond():
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > self.timeout_ms:
                raise OSError('VL53L1X timeout waiting for ' + what)
            time.sleep_ms(2)

    # ---- ranging control ----
    def start_ranging(self):
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_INTERRUPT_CLEAR, b'\x01')
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_MODE_START, b'\x40')  # continuous (timed) ranging

    def stop_ranging(self):
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_MODE_START, b'\x00')

    def clear_interrupt(self):
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_INTERRUPT_CLEAR, b'\x01')

    def data_ready(self):
        # Interrupt polarity: GPIO_HV_MUX__CTRL bit 4 = 0 means active high.
        pol = 0 if self._rd(_GPIO_HV_MUX_CTRL, 1)[0] & 0x10 else 1
        return (self._rd(_GPIO_TIO_HV_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x01) == pol

    # ---- settings ----
    def distance_mode(self):
        v = self._rd(_PHASECAL_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP, 1)[0]
        return 1 if v == 0x14 else 2 if v == 0x0A else None

    def set_distance_mode(self, mode):
        """1 = short (up to ~1.3 m, better in sunlight), 2 = long (up to 4 m in the dark)."""
        tb = getattr(self, '_tb', 50)
        if mode == 1:
            self._wr(_PHASECAL_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP, b'\x14')
            self._wr(_RANGE_CONFIG_VCSEL_PERIOD_A, b'\x07')
            self._wr(_RANGE_CONFIG_VCSEL_PERIOD_B, b'\x05')
            self._wr(_RANGE_CONFIG_VALID_PHASE_HIGH, b'\x38')
            self._wr(_SD_CONFIG_WOI_SD0, b'\x07\x05')
            self._wr(_SD_CONFIG_INITIAL_PHASE_SD0, b'\x06\x06')
        elif mode == 2:
            self._wr(_PHASECAL_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP, b'\x0A')
            self._wr(_RANGE_CONFIG_VCSEL_PERIOD_A, b'\x0F')
            self._wr(_RANGE_CONFIG_VCSEL_PERIOD_B, b'\x0D')
            self._wr(_RANGE_CONFIG_VALID_PHASE_HIGH, b'\xB8')
            self._wr(_SD_CONFIG_WOI_SD0, b'\x0F\x0D')
            self._wr(_SD_CONFIG_INITIAL_PHASE_SD0, b'\x0E\x0E')
        else:
            raise ValueError('distance mode must be 1 (short) or 2 (long)')
        self.set_timing_budget(tb if tb in (_TB_SHORT if mode == 1 else _TB_LONG) else 50)

    def set_timing_budget(self, ms):
        """15 (short only), 20, 33, 50, 100, 200 or 500 ms."""
        table = _TB_SHORT if self.distance_mode() == 1 else _TB_LONG
        if ms not in table:
            raise ValueError('unsupported timing budget for this distance mode')
        a, b = table[ms]
        self._wr16(_RANGE_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_A_HI, a)
        self._wr16(_RANGE_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_B_HI, b)
        self._tb = ms

    def set_inter_measurement_ms(self, ms):
        """Period between ranges in continuous mode; must be >= the timing budget."""
        d = self._rd(_RESULT_OSC_CALIBRATE_VAL, 2)
        pll = ((d[0] << 8) | d[1]) & 0x3FF
        v = int(pll * ms * 1.075)
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_INTERMEASUREMENT_PERIOD, bytes(((v >> 24) & 0xFF, (v >> 16) & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF)))

    def set_address(self, new_addr):
        self._wr(_I2C_SLAVE_DEVICE_ADDRESS, bytes((new_addr & 0x7F,)))
        self.addr = new_addr

    # ---- measurement ----
    def read(self):
        """Wait for the next range. Returns the distance in mm, or None if the range status
        is not valid (no target, signal too weak, out of range). Call start_ranging() first."""
        self._wait(self.data_ready, 'data')
        self.range_status = _STATUS.get(self._rd(_RESULT_RANGE_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x1F, 255)
        d = self._rd(_RESULT_RANGE_MM, 2)
        self.clear_interrupt()
        mm = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        return mm if self.range_status == 0 else None

# VL53L1X time-of-flight distance sensor (VL53L1X)

## Overview
The **VL53L1X** from STMicroelectronics is a FlightSense time-of-flight ranging sensor. It fires 940 nm infrared laser pulses (Class 1, eye-safe) and times the reflections, giving an absolute distance in millimetres from about 4 cm up to 4 m (long mode, dark, white target).
- Distance modes: short (up to about 1.3 m, better in sunlight) and long (up to 3.6–4 m in the dark, but only about 0.73 m in strong ambient light).
- Timing budget 20–1000 ms per range (33 ms is the minimum for long mode); up to 50 Hz.
- Field of view 27° (programmable down to 15° with a smaller ROI).
- Modelled board: **Adafruit VL53L1X Time of Flight Distance Sensor (product 3967)**. It has an LP5907 2.8 V regulator, BSS138 level shifting on SDA/SCL/XSHUT, 10 kΩ pull-ups and two STEMMA QT connectors.

## Pinout (Adafruit 3967, header order)
| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | Supply, 3–5 V (regulated to 2.8 V on the board) |
| GND | Ground |
| SCL | I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up, level shifted) |
| SDA | I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up, level shifted) |
| GPIO | Interrupt output (GPIO1), 2.8 V logic, data-ready |
| XSHUT | Shutdown input, active low, level shifted |

## Electrical limits
- Bare chip AVDD: 2.6–3.5 V (typ. 2.8 V). Never put more than 3.5 V on a bare module; the Adafruit board's regulator takes 3–5 V on VIN.
- Current: 16 mA typical, 18 mA max while ranging; peaks up to 40 mA. HW standby (XSHUT low) about 5 µA.
- I2C up to 400 kHz. Operating temperature −20 to 85 °C. Boot takes up to 1.2 ms after XSHUT goes high.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x29** (7-bit; the datasheet gives the 8-bit form 0x52). Change it in software through register 0x0001; it resets on power-up or XSHUT.
- **16-bit register addresses**, sent MSB first; data is big-endian.
- ID: 0x010F = **0xEA** (model ID), 0x0110 = 0xCC (module type), 0x0111 = 0x10 (mask revision).
- Init (ST Ultra Lite Driver): wait for 0x00E5 bit 0 = 1 (booted), write the 91-byte default configuration to 0x002D–0x0087, start ranging (0x0086 = 0x01, 0x0087 = 0x40), wait for data ready, clear the interrupt, stop (0x0087 = 0x00), then 0x0008 = 0x09 and 0x000B = 0x00.
- Data ready: GPIO__TIO_HV_STATUS 0x0031 bit 0 equals the interrupt polarity (active high when 0x0030 bit 4 is 0, the default).
- Result: 0x0096–0x0097 = distance in **mm** (16-bit unsigned, big-endian). 0x0089 bits 4:0 = range status; 9 means valid.
- After each reading write 0x01 to SYSTEM__INTERRUPT_CLEAR (0x0086); the next result is not updated until you do.
- ST publishes no full register map; the driver follows ST's ULD API (STSW-IMG009) as used by Adafruit's library.

## Wiring
| Breakout | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| VIN | 3V3 | 3V3(OUT) pin 36 | 3.3 V pin 1 |
| GND | GND | GND pin 38 | GND pin 6 |
| SDA | GPIO21 | GP4 (pin 6) | GPIO2 SDA pin 3 |
| SCL | GPIO22 | GP5 (pin 7) | GPIO3 SCL pin 5 |
| XSHUT | optional GPIO | optional GPIO | optional GPIO |
| GPIO | optional GPIO (IRQ) | optional GPIO | optional GPIO |

On a Raspberry Pi 4 running Linux use `adafruit-circuitpython-vl53l1x` instead of this MicroPython driver.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from vl53l1x import VL53L1X

i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(4), scl=Pin(5), freq=400000)   # Pico
tof = VL53L1X(i2c)          # long mode, 50 ms timing budget
tof.start_ranging()
while True:
    mm = tof.read()          # None when the range status is not valid
    print('out of range' if mm is None else 'D=%d mm' % mm)
    time.sleep_ms(200)
```
`tof.set_distance_mode(1)` switches to short mode; `tof.set_timing_budget(100)` trades speed for range and repeatability. `tof.range_status` holds the last ULD status (0 = valid, 1 = sigma fail, 2 = signal fail, 4 = out of bounds, 7 = wrap-around).

**Several sensors on one bus:** hold every XSHUT low, release one, create `VL53L1X(i2c)` and call `set_address(0x30)`, then release the next and give it another address.

## Gotchas
- **Peel off the protective film** over the sensor window first.
- Below 4 cm the sensor still detects a target but the distance is not accurate.
- Sunlight and other IR shorten long-mode range sharply (to about 73 cm); use short mode outdoors.
- The address returns to 0x29 at every power cycle or XSHUT reset.
- No offset or crosstalk calibration is done here; a cover glass needs ST's calibration flow.
- The driver uses `writeto`/`readfrom` with a two-byte register address, so it works on MicroPython ports whose `readfrom_mem` lacks `addrsize=16`.

## Datasheet
https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/vl53l1x.pdf (mirror used: https://www.pololu.com/file/0J1506/vl53l1x.pdf)
